To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the theory of the rise to prominence of the large industrial corporation as presented by Alfred Chandler can be rescued from its current state of near irrelevance by placing the development of managerial practices earlier in the historical sequence than Chandler himself did, and by relying on a wider variety of evidence to support the theory.

(1) the most influential theory on the rise of the modern corporation, that of Alfred Chandler, is not as flawed as critics suggest, and (2) the theory can be salvaged by relying on data from other sources, especially those that are not based on the Chandlerian paradigm.
